simple.meaning: כִּלְאַיִם (kilʼayim) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “two heterogeneities.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 4 times across Leviticus, Deuteronomy, beginning at Leviticus 19:19. Its meaning is built by comparing the passages where Scripture uses it.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כִּלְאַיִם (H3610).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: כִּלְאַיִם (kilʼayim) / H3610 is traced through Leviticus 19:19, Deuteronomy 22:9 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.full: H3610. kilayim כִּלְאַיִם noun [masculine] dual two kinds (Arabic , both ; Ethiopic two ; perhaps also כלאי MI 23 both, two , Nö LCB 1889, 61, cf Dr Sm xcii ; Sm u. So MI, 1886 suggest reservoirs ; see also כְּלִי ) — כ ׳תַּרְבִּיעַ לֹא בְּהֶמְתְּךָ Lev 19:19 not cause thy cattle to breed (in) two kinds ; כ תִּזְרַע לֹא ׳שָֽׂדְךָ 19:19 (H); כ ׳כַּרְמְךָ תִּזְרַע לֹא Deut 22:9 (both כִּלְאָ֑יִם ); כ ׳בֶּגֶד Lev 19:19 (H); — only in law of H and D against mixtures.
